pages.text: $(item)Filament Spools$() don't stack, so a drawer full of them clutters fast. The $(item)Filament Rack$() is a bookshelf-style shelf with $(l)8 slots$() (2×4) to store them.$(br2)Right-click the rack with a spool in hand to $(l)shelve$() it. Right-click with an empty hand to pop the $(l)last$() one back out: last in, first out.

pages.title: Visible Storage
pages.text: Shelved spools render on the $(l)front$() of the rack, each tinted with its $(l)tier color$(), and the shelf fills in visibly as you stock it.$(br2)It also emits a $(l)comparator signal$() scaled to how full it is.

pages.title: Filament Reservoir
pages.text: A rack is also a $(l)Filament Unit reservoir$(). When a printer or fabricator runs out of its own docked spools mid-print, it automatically pulls Filament Units from a rack that's $(l)touching$() it, or wired to it with an $(item)MC3D Cable$().$(br2)Docked spools always feed $(l)first$(); the rack is the reserve. Down-only tier rules apply: a higher-tier spool can pay lower-tier costs, never the reverse.
The Filament Rack. Keep one next to every printer as a backup tank of Filament Units.
